question: Question linked to image nº3 58-year-old liver transplant patient with HCV + cirrhosis. After an uncomplicated postoperative period, the patient is referred to his home. Six weeks after the transplant, he was visited in the outpatient clinic, with a low grade of fever, a worsening of the general condition, a GOT level of 60 IU / L (8-40) and a GPT of 65 IU / L (8-50). with a pattern of marked cholestasis (GGT x 10 and FA x 8) with total bilirubin of 1.7 mg / dL (0.3-1). Likewise, a high number of copies of the HCV was appreciated. It was decided to perform a Doppler ultrasound in which a complete arterial thrombosis was reported. In view of these data, a CT scan and a cholangioresonance were requested, the images of which are presented in the figures. For the clinical, analytical and radiological data, indicate which is the most probable diagnosis of the current problem:

options.opa: Acute rejection mediated by antibodies with associated arterial thrombosis.
options.opd: Extensive ischemic injury of intrahepatic bile ducts.
options.ope: Complete thrombosis of intrahepatic portal branches.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Liver transplant" -> "HCV recurrence risk" -> "High HCV viral load" -> "Liver inflammation" -> "Elevated GOT and GPT" -> "Possible early HCV recurrence" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Liver transplant" -> "Risk of vascular complications" -> "Arterial thrombosis" -> "Ischemic injury" -> "Cholestasis pattern" -> "Extensive ischemic injury of intrahepatic bile ducts" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Liver transplant" -> "Risk of rejection" -> "Antibody-mediated rejection" -> "Arterial thrombosis" -> "Cholestasis pattern" -> "Acute rejection mediated by antibodies with associated arterial thrombosis" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Liver transplant" -> "Biliary anastomosis risk" -> "Stenosis" -> "Cholestasis pattern" -> "Elevated GGT and FA" -> "Stenosis of the biliary anastomosis" -> 60%

CHAIN: "Liver transplant" -> "Portal vein thrombosis risk" -> "Complete thrombosis of intrahepatic portal branches" -> "Possible ischemic injury" -> "Cholestasis pattern" -> "Complete thrombosis of intrahepatic portal branches" -> 65%
analysis: The patient, a liver transplant recipient, presents with fever, elevated liver enzymes, and marked cholestasis six weeks post-transplant. The Doppler ultrasound shows complete arterial thrombosis. These findings suggest a vascular complication leading to ischemic injury. The elevated liver enzymes and cholestasis pattern, along with the arterial thrombosis, are consistent with extensive ischemic injury of the intrahepatic bile ducts, rather than acute rejection, HCV recurrence, biliary anastomosis stenosis, or portal thrombosis.
